changed.what: Applied F-U38a's request: step 6 now says the commit that records the frob-units hatch open removes conditional_on = "BD-031: escape-hatch" from KA-779's derivation file (else N38a-13 keeps reporting not-run: conditional and the opened row can never be bound); the acceptance item and an e2e assert check the key against the recorded decision by reading the front matter, since N38a-13's runner is M1 and not a dependency. N33-KA moved from related to deps (the derivation file must exist; level 13 under 27). Took the two items moved from N33c-07 and N33c-02 (they waited on this bead, which depends on them): the admission record carries the gate-time survey hash and diffs and the coupling record's hash and headline counts, citing only a coupling record made at the lock's FD-FSIM git_rev. The e2e script now runs the survey and coupling steps it was said to own. The ADR's list of pins a train must move is read from the survey (consumed siblings in not_on_candidate_a), as N33c-07 says. Step 7 no longer implies the script writes gates.toml: tier run with --features gauntlet-mutations, N33a-07 record with harness_receipt, record_gate by a non-implementing session (convention 9).

C11-std was right: the harness writes its e2e lines through scripts/e2e/lib.sh but did not depend on STD-E2E; added. Resumption skipped any recorded cell, so a not-run cell (lane missing, install failed) was never retried and a half-run matrix looked finished; now only pass and fail are skipped, the harness exits non-zero when a run cell has no record, and the per-cell timeout is a flag --timeout-s (default 3600) so the timeout test runs in seconds; new test not_run_is_retried.

Start-ready note applied (evidence holds: BD-001 was used only for the lock's git_rev): the script takes --rev <sha>, else the lock's FD-FSIM git_rev, else exits 3; the record states rev_source; deps now [] (ready at hour 0), BD-001 to related. Acceptance item 4 (counts and hash in the INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 record) moved to BD-031, which depends on this bead (it waited on its own dependent, convention 7). The script is named (scripts/admission/qty_coupling.sh) so BD-031 can call it, and the unit fixture is a scratch git repo passed with --repo; new test revision_source. C11-std is a false alarm: the e2e run is BD-031's.

Start-ready note applied (evidence holds: BD-001 was used only to read the lock): --stack-lock <path> (default franken-stack.lock); with no lock the survey says so, records stack_lock: null and treats every sibling as consumed (fail-closed, exit 3); deps now [], BD-001 to related. Consumed is now read from every posture form the lock allows (the posture key or any uses entry of consume, consume-path or build-time), so a build-time sibling's drift is no longer missed. The item attaching the first diff to the INT-TOOLCHAIN-01 record moved to BD-031 (convention 7). New test no_lock_is_fail_closed. C11-std is a false alarm (the e2e run is BD-031's).

F-U33b's request applied: the train-log plant uses kind = "pin" (N33b-04's closed set rejects compat, so the test could never pass). Condition 3 named only consume-path rows, which left the frankensympy build-time use (NF-04) and the consume rows of N33a-03 unchecked against the one-toolchain rule; it now covers every use of consume, consume-path or build-time that has a sibling checkout (path and 40-hex git_rev), with the test extended. The e2e script now runs each plant against the other five checks, which the 'no other check' acceptance item asks for and nothing ran.

Audit note applied (evidence holds: the six checks are assembled by BD-004, which this bead does not reach): acceptance item 'each plant is caught by check-deps and by no other of the six checks' and the summary count of plants caught by another check are removed here and requested of N34-14, whose workspace_checks.sh runs all six checks; the e2e section says so. The register text now matches the rows the bead adds (four non-survey siblings and franken-kernel with survey = false). Restored the blank line before Test plan, which the section parser needs.

Acceptance item 2 required capabilities to print a 'referee mode remote' field that no schema defines, and the group listing it implied is N33c-32's, which depends on this bead (convention 7). It now checks what this bead builds: the remote build's cargo tree names no volatile fs-* crate and frob_fsim::BUILT_WITH is empty, with test remote_build_compiles_no_group.

H-verbs-5's request applied: item 7 states that VERBS-operator's capabilities row carries --require-group <group> and needs_groups = [{ from_argument = "require_group" }], written by this bead in the change that adds the field. --allow-unadmitted was used on every verb but declared nowhere, so NJL-01's common-property-shadowed lint and the strict parser would refuse it; it is now a process option added to NJL-01's PROCESS_OPTIONS by this bead, with test allow_unadmitted_is_a_process_option. F-U37's request (rename conformance.probe) needs nothing: the bead no longer has that verb and tests through capabilities --require-group.

The ADR recorded only the share rule's readings (recorded, lift considered, referee-speed finding, readiness), none of which is one of N40-03's four outcomes, so the KILL-FSIM row's M2 entry (rolling, due at M2) could not be written and the loader would refuse it. New step 6: the M2 entry's outcome comes from the registered trigger re-read with N33b-05's reader scripts/decide/kill_fsim.sh (hold → not-fired, fire → fired, blocked → deferred), and the share reading is recorded beside it as a finding that is not a trigger; N33b-05 added to deps (M0, level 28; the reader must exist); the acceptance item names the entry and the loader. The e2e called fidelity.shadow with a positional action word (start, status), which NJL-01 rules out; now --action start and --action status, without a key (an admin verb).

The one-package check used cargo tree -d -e dev, which shows dev edges only and so would hide a second asupersync reached by a normal edge: now cargo tree -d (all edges). Its e2e step 3 called xtask check-deps for a 'no non-dev edge enables full-runtime' rule that no check-deps bead implements (convention 8); now cargo tree -e no-dev,features -i asupersync must show no full-runtime node, also in the acceptance item. The sleep-refused negative control named no command and no mechanism: the outcome gains Refused { reason }, the harness refuses a poll that blocks more than 100 ms of wall time while virtual time stands still, with unit test sleep_in_program_refused that the e2e step runs. The probe step passed two test filters to cargo test without --, which cargo rejects.

Acceptance item 6 checked that cargo tree of the frob binaries 'does not contain the module's feature', a feature that exists nowhere; it now checks that cargo tree -p frob -e no-dev and cargo tree -p frobd -e no-dev name no frob-conformance, the crate that holds the stub.

The gate row is entered from the receipt of the gate's tier run, but the e2e script never ran that tier nor wrote the admission record; new step 6 runs e2e_tier <tier> INT-ASUP-02 --mutations, logs the receipt hash and writes the N33a-07 record with that harness_receipt, record_gate left to a non-implementing session (convention 9). Half one's 100 fresh-process runs named no command: new unit test half_one_run, run by the script in 100 processes under FROB_TEST_SEED.

Acceptance item 5 required the policy to run in shadow beside LRU in the store's statistics and be switched by one flag; the policy switch memo.policy and its shadow setting are N33c-19's, which depends on this bead (convention 7). The item now checks what this bead builds (the state machine and an LRU reference reporting both hit ratios on one stream) and names N33c-19 for the switch; step 5 names the flag's owner.

The gate row is entered from the receipt of the gate's tier run with the planted mutants as controls, but the e2e script never ran that tier nor wrote the admission record; new step 5 runs e2e_tier <tier> INT-FSQL-02 --mutations, logs the receipt hash and writes the N33a-07 record with that harness_receipt, record_gate left to a non-implementing session.

On dropped-by-ceiling the bead entered a gates.toml row 'not run with reason dropped-by-ceiling' through record_gate, which records only a receipt's pass or fail (N38b-19) and has no such status; now the admission record carries the reason with status not-run and harness_receipt null, and the gate row gets no part and reads not-run (N40-01). The gate was to be recorded 'by this bead, the one that measures it', which N38b-19 refuses as self-certified; now by a session that did not implement the extractor. The e2e script now runs the gate's tier (e2e_tier <tier> INT-FJAX-01 --mutations) whose receipt the recorder cites.
The e2e ran frob spark check --backend <b> with no kernel selector; VERBS-spark's row selects kernels with --kernel or --all (BD-176), so the regenerated library is now checked with --all.

F-U32b's request applied: on do not fund the pilot result's verdict is falsifier-holds and the funding session closes N32b-06 to N32b-09 withdrawn citing the pilot and that result (N41-17 rule 7); KILL-TUI's decision N32b-31, which depends on N32b-09, then becomes ready and is taken from the pilot's record alone instead of waiting for ever on dashboard replays that cannot exist. Scope now names N32b-06 to N32b-09 (it said -08). The gate row had no recording form: the admission record now cites the gate tier's receipt, the part is entered with record_gate by a session that did not implement the probe, and the e2e runs e2e_tier <tier> INT-FTUI-01 --mutations.

INT-FDGR-01 has two parts (M3 and M5, N40-02), but the bead recorded it with record_gate without --part and 'by this bead', which N38b-19 refuses as self-certified; now --part M3, by a session that did not implement the adapter, with the M5 part left not-run for BD-398. The admission record cites the tier run's receipt, and the e2e script now runs e2e_tier <tier> INT-FDGR-01 --mutations; the record counts eight fixture outcomes, not five.

The e2e summary named gates: [INT-FMCP-01 (facts only)], which is not a gate identifier and would enter STD-E2E's gate report as a measured gate this bead does not measure; the summary's gates list is now empty, the record that cites the facts being BD-023's.

The gate part was to be entered by 'this bead, the one that measures the gate', which N38b-19 refuses as self-certified, and the bead did not reach N38b-19 at all; N38b-19 added to deps (level 12 under 14, no level change), the part is entered by a session that implemented neither the worker nor the candidate, and with no candidate no part is recorded (the recorder has no not-run status) so the row reads not-run while the admission record carries the reason. The e2e script runs e2e_tier <tier> INT-FTX-01 --mutations when a candidate exists.

H-owners-2's request applied: stack.gate-receipt follows a part's receipt that is a receipt set (frob.gauntlet.receipt-set/1) to its members and applies the resolution and dirty-tree conditions to each member's stack receipt, so a multi-tier pass can no longer hide a dirty member; new plant E with test inv_suite_03_receipt_set_members, the e2e running five plants. C13 finding fixed: the 'DESIGN here, requested of N40-01' narration about receipts/gates/<hash>.json now states the owners' form (N38b-19 step 9; N40-01 'Where receipts live'). N38b-19, the owner of the receipt-set format, added to deps (level 12 under 14, no level change).

The description of suite_ws06.sh's --sampler-row summary named 'GATE-WS-06 (sampler row)', not a gate identifier; it now lists GATE-WS-06 (part M2) and GATE-CORTEX-18 by identifier, as STD-E2E's summary format requires.
The e2e section added steps to scripts/e2e/suite_deps_rules.sh without naming its owner (convention 11); it now names N33c-09, a dependency.

The bead wrote msl_version into the INT-FT-01 admission record, which is BD-016's (a dependency; admission records are append-only and BD-016 already records the language version); msl_version now lives in this bead's facts record and must equal the version in BD-016's record, a difference being a changed fact. Scope, acceptance and the e2e assert follow.

Row 8 and its acceptance item said the INT-FT-01 admission record carries msl_version, which neither BD-016 nor N33c-39 writes there; they now read N33c-39's facts record and compare it with BD-016's recorded language version.

H-cx-2's request applied: N33-CX's FACT entry suite-reduced-catalog names this bead's GATE-WS-09 probe record as its re-run, but nothing set the flag, so its control stayed an obligation runnable for no gate. New step 6 (BD-033's pattern): when the record reproduces 30 links and 31.96314202 kg, a session that did not implement the probe sets rerun = true and rerun_receipt to the record's receipt hash, changes no other field and re-runs N38b-05's seeding tool; another total leaves the entry unchanged and flags the fact changed. Acceptance item and scratch-catalogue test added. N33-CX added to deps (the entry and the seeding tool must exist; level 14 under 25, no level change).

H-cx-2's request applied: new step 6 sets rerun = true and rerun_receipt on N33-CX's FACT entry suite-power-detects-sign when the probe reproduces (12, −8) and (−12, 8), by a session that did not implement the probe, then re-runs N38b-05's seeding tool so the entry's control becomes runnable; other rates leave the entry unchanged and flag the fact changed. Acceptance item and scratch-catalogue test added. N33-CX added to deps (level 14 to 15; no dependent's level changes).

The M2 part of GATE-WS-09 was to be entered 'by the recording session' with no condition on who that is; N38b-19 refuses self-certified, so the agent that implements the probe would be refused. It now says a session that did not implement this probe or the other M2 row.

H-cx-2's request applied: new step 7 sets rerun = true and rerun_receipt on N33-CX's FACT entry suite-float-bound when the record reproduces both returned values (1.0 and 1.0, both not-a-bound), by a session that did not implement the probe, then re-runs N38b-05's seeding tool; a differing value (for example probe 2 fixed upstream) leaves the entry unchanged and flags the fact changed. Acceptance item and scratch-catalogue test added. N33-CX added to deps (level 13 to 15; no dependent's level changes).
As in N33c-44: the M2 part is entered by a session that did not implement this probe or the other M2 row (N38b-19 refuses self-certified), never by the script.

The M0 and M2 parts of GATE-WS-09 were entered by 'the recording session' with no condition, so the agent that writes the four G1 entries would run record_gate and be refused as self-certified (N38b-19); item 6 and the acceptance item now require a session that implemented none of the probes or entries the part covers.

requests.what: Moved here from N33c-09 by the graph audit: add N33c-09 to deps (no level change, 14 stays 14) and carry N33c-09's plants (its acceptance items 2, 4, 5 and 6: asupersync 0.5.0, frankentui executor, never-dependency sibling, posture register) as extra-plant rows of scripts/e2e/workspace_checks.sh, asserting each is reported by check-deps and by no other of the six checks, with the summary counting plants caught by another check. N33c-09 cannot assert it: the six checks are assembled by BD-004, which it does not reach.

The fidelity.shadow row's machine-field example is `frob fidelity shadow start --job j:77c0 --p 0.002 --cpu-cores 24 --tier referee --json`, a positional action word that NJL-01 rules out (the row's own Inputs say the action is the input property `action`); write `frob fidelity shadow --action start --job j:77c0 --p 0.002 --cpu-cores 24 --tier referee --json`.
